content_text_body:
Research shows that executives and management can improve safety through more direct interactions with frontline workers.  [Leadership walkrounds](https://psnet.ahrq.gov/issue/patient-safety-leadership-walkrounds)-visits by management to clinical units in order to engage in frank discussion around safety concerns-can positively impact safety culture.

### Why is it important?

Frontline employees have great insights into the patient "experience."  They also are very familiar with processes, procedures, and the way care actually gets delivered in a given area.  They can spot problems or unsafe behaviors that could eventually bring harm to patients.  Seeking out their feedback and advice and making sure there is structured and timely response to their feedback is important in helping you build your desired culture for safety.  These rounding sessions also engage frontline employees in the solution and help demonstrate leaders' commitment to safety.  

**The Institute for Healthcare Improvement released guidelines for Patient Safety WalkRoundsâ„¢. A summary of their suggestions are below:**

- **Leaders should conduct these safety rounds at least once a week for one hour**  
Building consistency with these conversations is important for you to develop trust with front-line workers and understand more about the culture of safety in the area. These can be rescheduled but they shouldn't canceled

- **Keep discussions focused on safety, don't diminish the importance of safety by trying to cover other topics**

- **Involve all the senior executives in the organization, not just the CEO**

- **Communicate with managers so they understand why senior executives are visiting their areas**

- **Make sure that senior executives follow up and provide feedback to staff about issues raised during the WalkRoundsâ„¢**   
According to the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, issues raised by frontline staff during WalkroundsTM must be promptly addressed, lest staff view the rounds as simply a visibility exercise for leadership

- **Institute regular safety briefings**  
Pass along issues raised in the briefings (with names of the contributing staff members withheld) to the executives to talk about on their WalkRoundsâ„¢

- **Take a digital camera. It has been wonderful for PowerPoint presentations to staff and quality council meetings. Pictures are worth a thousand words. [Submitted by Marie Zappia Kuzmack, San Clemente Hospital]**

- **Prior to leaving the unit, have executives summarize the issues and ask staff to prioritize 2 to 3 items to be addressed. [Submitted by: Eunice Jones, Catholic Healthcare Partners, Knoxville, TN]**

- **Managers should also have frequent huddles and briefings with their teams about patient safety to improve the quality and frequency of communications**

- **An excellent sample PDF agenda for these "Huddles" is available for [download](http://www.ihi.org/resources/Pages/Tools/Patient-Safety-Essentials-Toolkit.aspx).  This Huddles PDF document is free from the Institute for Healthcare Improvement by registering on the site**

>Source: 

>"Leadership Role in Improving Safety." Patient Safety Network Primer.  Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality.
